In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data do not favour the hypothesis of primary cosmic ray particles of energy 10 15 eV or higher being protons or helium nuclei.
the primary cosmic rays of > 10 15 eV energy consist of protons, helium nuclei and heavier nuclei in the ratio 0.5 : 0.3 : 0.2.
the experiment is consistent with the assumption that the primaries are protons and that their spectrum falls off as E −2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have obtained the first direct evidence for a new component of cosmic rays with energies above 10 15 eV.
the results of the Kolar experiment have established the existence of a flux of primary particles of energies in excess of 10 18 eV.
the results are consistent with the hypothesis that the primary particles are protons and the energy spectrum is steeper than E −3, with the exponent varying between 3.5 and 3.8.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a large number of high energy muons are produced in the atmosphere by primary cosmic ray particles of energies > 10 15 eV and that their angular correlation with the shower axis is not random.
the experiment was successful in demonstrating that it was possible to obtain a high precision estimate of the shower parameters in showers of very small sizes.
the muon density at ground level in showers of energy > 5×10 17 eV can be accurately estimated by using the measured shower parameters and the atmospheric profile.
